title: Reject oversized SCHC fragments before attacker-tail integer conversion
description: Security review finding in python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py Fragment.from_bytes: after checking only a two-byte minimum, the decoder converts the entire attacker-controlled tail with int.from_bytes before enforcing a maximum profile wire length. A caller that receives data outside an already MTU-bounded link can be forced to allocate and process arbitrarily large integers, creating avoidable CPU and memory exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria: Fragment.from_bytes derives the maximum legal encoded Fragment length from the profile header/padding, optional RCS, and maximum 187-byte tile, and rejects longer input before int.from_bytes or any proportional large-integer work. Boundary tests accept the exact maximum legal encoding, reject maximum-plus-one, and reject a very large attacker-controlled buffer through the early bounded path. Existing canonical padding and field validation remain intact. Run three independent correctness, security, and robustness code-review passes and file every resulting finding before closure.
